entry.title: Round Lakes
entry.content: While working with the LAGOS database, I have realized that there are many lakes with the name “Round Lake”, many of which I would not actually describe as round. After seeing an animation on r/dataisbeautiful, I made this gif for fun in RStudio. It takes every lake in the LAGOS database with the name “Round Lake” and sorts them in increasing order of roundness using the lakes’ shoreline development index (the ratio of the length of the lake’s shoreline to the circumference of a circle with the same area as the lake). I don’t think there’s really a practical use for this, but it’s a fun visualization!

entry.title: DILLLYMPICS
entry.content:
One fateful day in the summer of 2025, I decided to take a break from coding by snooping around the lab to see what was hiding in our seldom-opened drawers and cabinets. Among old t-shirts and miscellaneous cords, I struck gold– literally (well, kind of). I found an unlabeled bag full of plastic gold, silver, and bronze medals. No one in the lab had a clue why or by whom the medals had been purchased, and it was clear that they had no intended purpose in our lab other than collecting dust in a drawer. At the time, our group was known as the DILL Lab (for Data Intensive Landscape Limnology), and we had recently learned that two members of the lab would soon be moving on to other opportunities. This finding could mean only one thing: we had to have the DILLLympics as a final send-off.

Over the next couple of months, I budgeted some time to personalize our plastic medals and polled the lab to decide on our DILLLympics events. We decided on: 1) an iNaturalist race to get the most observations in a given time period 2) a worst figure competition (in good fun) 3) ping-pong, and 4) a “DILL” themed snack contest.

On November 16th, a day that will go down in the history books, we met at Kendra’s house for the competitions. Tough battles were fought intermittently between snacking and socialization. We documented the species around the property, witnessed Kendra’s fierce ping-pong skills, had some laughs at a few very creatively designed figures, and enjoyed many dill flavored foods. We also watched Kendra’s family turtle ride a skateboard around the house (very impressive) and made custom DILL Lab shirts using a couple of linocut designs I made. Overall, it was a great time and a fitting bon voyage for our departing colleagues.

left: My prized gold medal from the iNaturalist competition. middle: some of the linocuts that we used to make t-shirts. right: The t-shirt I made

entry.title: Trivia
entry.content:
In high school, I became a very big fan of Jeopardy!, to the point that I once made my family go see Alex Trebek host the show while we were on vacation in LA. In my adult life, my love of quiz competition has taken a more active role in the form of Sporcle bar trivia. My friends at the UofM Biostation got me into bar trivia for the first time at a pub in Pellston (which was actually inside of the airport), and we had so much fun that we kept our team going back in Ann Arbor. When I came to MSU, I noticed a distinct lack of trivia in the grad student community. I decided to fix that by sending out a message to the grad students in my departments and creating a new team for anyone who wanted to join. I’ve made some of my closest friends at MSU through our trivia team and will even say that we’re not half bad! We now look forward to trivia Tuesdays every week and have learned an assortment of fun facts across a range of topics. We just learned that there are actually regional and national bar trivia competitions through Sporcle and are formally registering our team so that we can compete– maybe we’ll make it big this fall!

left: Our first time winning two rounds of trivia in one night! This was back in our earlier days. right: A more recent picture of our team all wearing pins of my friend's cat. We're now big enough to need two tables!

entry.title: Filmography
entry.content:
The University of Michigan Biological Station is a place that inspires me, both scientifically and creatively. When I was working there as a field technician in 2024, the sounds of waves crashing on the shore of the lake would sometimes remind me of one of my favorite films, The Lighthouse (2019, Robert Eggers). I pitched to my friends the possibility of making a tribute to the film and by the next day, we had a (rough) script adapted from the original. It would be a surreal Biostation-themed parody in which “the lighthouse” was the belltower that the kitchen staff at the station would ring to announce meals. I pushed my novice (i.e. nonexistent) directing skills to their limits while co-starring and editing our footage. When we finally had it ready, we screened The Belltower to an audience on the last day of classes at the station. Despite only having filmed in our free time over two weeks, some of my friends delivered pretty stellar performances.

A year later, I went with some friends to visit the Biostation again for a few days. My costar from the first film had been watching a lot of X-files and I was really into Werner Herzog at the time, so we decided this trip would be a perfect opportunity to make another film. This time, it was a mystery/thriller that drew heavy inspiration from the X-files and Herzog’s found footage “Incident at Loch Ness” as well as the cryptic Douglas Lake Monster that we had heard tales of at the station. For our second film, we had no script other than a loose outline of our plot, and we recruited almost everyone we came across as actors. The Dougie Files ended up having a much broader appeal (and possibly more cultural relevance) than our first endeavor and was incredibly fun to make. We even drew on a couple of ecological concepts for parts of our story.

Due to their PG-13 ratings, I won’t make my films too easy to find on this site. If you’re interested in watching them, you can find them on my Youtube channel, @KendallAsh-e2b.

left: Our first screening of The Belltower! middle: The official Dougie Files poster. right: A candid shot of us trying to figure out how to use the camera while filming with our prop of the Douglas Lake Monster.
